title: Canonical exterior cohomology of a derived algebra
statement: Let $R$ be a commutative ring and $K$ an object of $D(R)$ [def-weil-abstract-derived-category], with unit $u:R[0]\to K$ and multiplication $\mu:K\otimes_R^{\mathbf L}K\to K$. Represent each $x\in H^n(K)$ by the unique derived morphism $R[-n]\to K$ inducing $1\mapsto x$, and define its cup product with $y\in H^q(K)$ by tensoring these representatives and composing with $\mu$, using the canonical signed single-tensor identification. Define the empty product to be the class of $u$ and products of degree-one classes by iteration. The predicate $\operatorname{IsExterior}(u,\mu)$ means that negative cohomology vanishes and there are $R$-linear isomorphisms $e_n:\bigwedge_R^n H^1(K)\simeq H^n(K)$ for every $n\ge0$, sending every pure wedge to the indicated product [def-weil-pbc-exterior-algebra]. For perfect $K$ [def-pc-perfect-ring-complex] and a ring map $R\to S$, define the scalar-extended unit and product using the inverse canonical coefficient-unit and balanced tensor comparisons of [lem-sf-perfect-scalar-tensor-coherence], followed by scalar extension of $u$ and $\mu$.
